note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 against HEAD c8584247bb (independent judge, clean clone). Supersedes the 'unimplemented' verdict, whose producers (apply.go::reloadPool, eap/pool.go::Allocate) were deleted in 14d83a90bd. Section 5.1: "Because SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3, it can become confused about where to send packets coming from Suzy's server.  Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring." POOL-BOUND PATH, enforced: assignVirtualIP leases one address per owner from the engine-wide eap.Registry, substituteVirtualIP narrows every proposed TSi to the lease host inside the proposal and refuses a bound peer holding no lease, proposeLeasedChildTSPayloads/answerNamesOnlyLeases keep a ze-initiated rekey on the lease, and ValidateVirtualIPPoolBindings refuses overlapping pools. TestTwoPeersSameRequestedAddressDistinctLeases asserts two distinct leases and two distinct NegotiatedTSi for two peers asking 10.10.0.3; TestNoChildSAWithoutLeaseOnBoundPeer asserts no SA/TS/CP payload without a lease; TestRFC3948ZeInitiatedRekeyNamesOnlyTheLease asserts the rekey proposal and refuses pool-prefix, configured-prefix, wildcard and wrong-family answers (errTSWidened). All PASS at HEAD (./le job run, scoped -run). ./le rfc discriminate id RFC3948-5.1-1: four mutant records (assignVirtualIP, substituteVirtualIP, proposeChildTSPayloads, answerNamesOnlyLeases), none stale, none unproven. WHY WEAK: the MUST is not met for a peer bound to no pool, and no tagged test can go red for it. narrowSelectors treats an EMPTY configured traffic-selector list as allow-everything, so an unbound responder peer answers whatever inner TSi it proposes. Overlay probe in the clone (not committed): two unbound peers ari and bob, each proposing TSi 10.1.2.3/32 with TSr 0.0.0.0/0 and 192.0.2.10/32, both get err=nil and NegotiatedPairs 10.1.2.3/32 <-> 0.0.0.0/0 and 10.1.2.3/32 <-> 192.0.2.10/32. dataplane policyOwners.claim refuses only an IDENTICAL selector key across owners (PolicyOwnedError) and compares overlap for transport mode only, so both tunnel outbound policies install and traffic from 192.0.2.10 to 10.1.2.3 matches both: the Section 5.1 confusion. The row's Support remaining text ('A peer bound to no pool is held to the remote traffic selectors its configuration names') is false for a peer that configures none. Fix: either refuse at the responder a tunnel Child SA whose remote inner selector overlaps another peer's live tunnel remote selector when that selector came from the peer's proposal rather than the operator's configured prefixes, or narrow an unconfigured responder's TSi to the peer's observed address as strongSwan's %dynamic default does; tag a negative over two unbound peers. Until then the row needs a {partial} (Tested: pool-bound peers; Gap: unbound peers with empty or overlapping selectors; Producer: ts_narrow.go::narrowSelectors) and an honest Support remaining. Also stale: rfc/extraction/rfc3948.json reasons for RFC3948-5.1-1 still describe the deleted unreached Pool.Allocate/reloadPool gap.
